summary: SL-099 was opened as a medium bug fix. It fixed SC-130 (Get-Missing in tests/window/PoolWatch.ps1 now judges a guard stop before the interrupted branch). It also made Get-Net's table Ordinal, added 14 watched tags, and added a case-exact fitness rule with a 58-row corpus. It wrote the outcome-C record (docs/design/SL-099-outcome-c-redesign.md) with a frozen session-1 reading rule, and committed the spike-107 evidence. Nothing under src/ changed and nothing was measured on the host, so the tens-of-GB pool report is exactly where SL-095 left it: not claimed fixed, Q-188 open. The small bug cost 2 risk-spike laps, 2 design laps, 4 critique runs, 2 code-review laps and 3 validate laps. Two of those validate laps were lost to causes unrelated to the code.

payload.reason: Reflection on SL-099 at HEAD d2620fc. Validate #3 accepted; O-044/O-045 were waived to SC-252/SC-253, and O-054..O-056 to SC-249/SC-250/SC-251.

payload.estimate_error: Size was under-labelled; the risk tier was slightly high. "Bug fix, medium" covered three merged backlog items (the SL-095 follow-up row, SC-129, SC-130). The real defect was a ~10-line reorder (PoolWatch.ps1:460-478) with a repro written before design, and spike 106 proved its fix in the first design lap. Everything else was added by the rescope and the rework: the outcome-C record, harness hardening, 4 new tests/bugs scripts and 53 evidence files. The commit touched 73 files; the 53 evidence data files are most of that count. Nothing under src/ changed and no end-user behaviour moved, so medium risk was high for the code. The real cost drivers were process: build-check #1 halted asking for a rescope nobody could give, design attempt 1 was taken back for fork O-017, the critique ran 4 times, and validate ran 3 times.
what_went_wrong: The slice was opened as one medium bug fix over a merged row (SL-095 follow-up items 1-4, SC-129, SC-130). Build-check #1 halted asking a person to rescope. With the owner away, the engine narrowed it (build-check #2) and design attempt 1 rescoped it again. Lesson #344 said to split at open; it was not split.

Design attempt 1 was taken back because fork O-017 needed a measurement. That cost a second risk-spike lap, a second design, and critique runs #3-#4. Attempt 2 then shipped checks that could not pass as written. N1: 'equals the same case on a git worktree of 0feac0e' ignored the C-011 line number and boot age and the random case-<12 hex> folder names, which spike sc130 had already measured. N2: two of the three spike-107 evidence paths were wrong. Critique round 2 caught both, but nobody had run them before they were written down.

O-018 declared the class 'case-folding tag comparison spellings' closed on a regex rule. Code review then found three more members across its two rounds: capitalised operators on the unprefixed first entry, Compare-Object/Select-String, and quoted or indexed 'tag' (`$_['tag']`). All three were waived to SC-249/SC-250/SC-251. The static rule was a taste-level extra, and it cost the most review churn.

The build report contained two wrong statements that code review had to correct. It claimed 'P-003/P-004/C-056 also pass under powershell.exe', but PoolWatchCases' Invoke-Report always launches pwsh. It also listed 'committing the repro' as not built, though commit d2620fc included it. O-003 was discharged on evidence that did not exercise Get-Missing in 5.1; the validator had to prove it with a scratch edit.

Validate #1 halted at the engine's memory floor: free memory 2.7 GB against the 3.1 GB floor, with 2 acting runs overlapping. It produced no evidence. Validate #2 passed but halted on O-044 and O-045. Those are 'F1 is cold' and 'the cache survives to F2..F5'; no run of this slice can discharge them, because only a person's session 1 can. Validate #3 accepted them waived. Code review had predicted exactly this.
All 21 critique findings in attempt 2 (13 + 8) were disposed by a model and counted as untriaged. No person looked at any of them.

The user's symptom was not advanced. The record explains arm L's growth as Windows' metadata cache, but MS Q&A 5966064 shows the same tags at 24.4 GB after 47.41 h with no release, so Q-188 is still open and the 'no scanner change' decision is unverified at host scale.

learned.lesson: Every 'must-verify' row in a design's invariants becomes a verify obligation aimed at validate-slice. For a precondition only a person's true Restart can measure, that obligation can never be discharged. It holds validate for one lap and is then waived. When the check needs session 1 (the person's Restart run), do not list it as a must-verify invariant. Put it in filed_for_later with who=person, state it in the record, and say in the design that no loop stage can discharge it.
learned.evidence: validate-slice #2: 'passed, but 2 obligations (O-044, O-045) aimed at this stage are still open'. validate #3 accepted, and both were waived to SC-252/SC-253. In attempt 1 the same shape gave O-013..O-016, voided. Code review wrote 'unless retargeted to a person, validate will hold on them'. Lessons #344/#357 already said this for criteria, not for preconditions.

learned.lesson: When a backlog row merges a small repro-backed defect with a research or redesign item, open them as two slices. The defect here was 10 lines and was fixed and spike-proven in the first design lap. Everything that made this slice take 2 spikes, 2 designs, 4 critiques and 3 validates was the redesign record plus the optional hardening (the fitness rule, 14 tags, 4 test scripts, 53 evidence files). Size and tier from what the repro fails on, and file the rest separately.
learned.evidence: Repro tests/bugs/SL-099-GuardStopSurvivesInterrupt.Tests.ps1 failed 2 checks at the start and passed after the Get-Missing reorder. The commit changed 73 files, 53 of them spike-107 data. No src/ change. Build-check #1 halted asking for a person to rescope.

learned.lesson: A regex fitness entry over PowerShell source cannot close the class 'case-folding tag comparison'. The spelling space is open: operator case, cmdlets (Group-Object, Compare-Object, Select-String, Sort -Unique), quoted and indexed property names, and switch. Do not write 'class closed' on such a rule. The real guard is P-004's behavioural mutation: Tag() switched to -eq goes red with the NtfF column at 900, and a Get-Net back to [ordered]@{} goes red. If SC-249/SC-250/SC-251 are built, build them as one slice. Prefer one AST-level check in P-004, which already loads Get-Net through the parser, over a fourth batch of patterns.
learned.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:1172-1198 holds two entries. The corpus has 58 rows with 7 plants (S44-S50). Code review rounds 1 and 2 found 3 more families after the build had already added 3 patterns beyond the design's 4 (waived O-054, O-055, O-056). Validate's three mutants (interrupted-first, ordered@{}, -eq) all turned P-003/P-004 red.

learned.lesson: In tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1, functions that Write-Output inside code whose return value is consumed swallow the output. At 0feac0e no case printed any -Report text, because Invoke-Report and Invoke-Fixture echoed through Write-Output. Invoke-Report's Check still does, so its 'no line carries a judgement word' ok line is never printed, though a FAIL still counts. Any slice that compares -Report text against a baseline must first copy the tree's PoolWatchCases over the base copy, and compare only after normalising case-<12 hex>, the scratch parent, PoolWatch.ps1:<n> and boot age. C-011 is compared by exit code and ok/FAIL counts only.
learned.evidence: Build deviation: 'Invoke-Report and Invoke-Fixture now echo through Write-Host'. Critique N1 evidence from spike sc130. SL-099-ReportTextUnchanged.Tests.ps1 runs both trees from git archive 0feac0e. Code-review drift on Invoke-Report's Check.

learned.lesson: PoolWatchCases' Invoke-Report launches `pwsh` for -Report. A claim that 'P-003/P-004/C-056 pass under powershell.exe' therefore does not run Get-Missing or Format-Net in Windows PowerShell 5.1. Only the SL-099 repro (which picks its own host) and P-004's in-process Get-Net call do. To prove the 5.1 path, copy the cases and swap `& pwsh ... -Report` for `& powershell.exe ... -Report`, as the validator did. C-011 is already red under 5.1 at HEAD.
learned.evidence: Code-review drift on the build's claim. The validator's scratch copy ran P-003, P-004, C-056 and P-001 under 5.1, all passing. O-003 had been discharged on the repro plus the unverified claim.

learned.lesson: Do not describe the tens-of-GB report as explained. The record and the investigation call L's growth Windows' metadata cache, with about 1 per cold folder, about 0 warm, and freed under deep pressure. The pressure result was only at Sandbox scale (4 GB, at most 400,000 files, ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.1). The host has ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.9444, about 830k folders, and 31 GB. MS Q&A 5966064 shows the same tags at 24.4 GB combined (13,626 MB paged, 10,786 MB nonpaged) after 47.41 h with no release. The record's reading rule (d) is frozen before session 1, and changing it afterwards costs another true Restart. Anything that edits rule (d) or PoolWatch -Protocol has to land before session 1.
learned.evidence: Record (b) and (e); review m6 and N5/N6; spike 107 limits (4 GB, 400,000 files, no reparse/sparse, I1 skipped so no 600 s idle pairs); Q-188 still open; SC-229/SC-231/SC-241 open.

learned.lesson: Spike run folders do not survive in the places they are written, and the record's claims then become uncheckable. Spike 87's marks.jsonl, events.log, T.json and result.txt were gone from C:\WINDOWS\TEMP within days. This slice rescued only spike 107 (docs/design/SL-099-runs/spike-107-2026-10-12/, 53 files, 4.2 MB, hash-compared). Spike 106's five experiments and the investigation's host/Sandbox runs back record claims (b) and the 'no purge, no pressure step' decision, but the build's file list shows no copy of them. Copy a run folder into docs/design/<slice>-runs/ in the same slice whose design cites it.
learned.evidence: Survey: C:\WINDOWS\TEMP\sl095-o003-20261005-004311 holds only L\ (dirs.log, L.json, skips.log); the pool figures can no longer be checked. Build file list: the only runs folder added is spike-107-2026-10-12.

learned.lesson: Pricing a heavy test at design time (lesson #351) does not protect validate. Validate on this project runs the full suite (805 tests), C-052 (268 s, walks a 30,150-folder tree), a -Rehearse -Keep run, the rules harness and three mutants. Its first lap was stopped by the engine's whole-machine floor (2.7 GB free against 3.1 GB) while 2 acting runs overlapped. For slices touching tests/window or PoolWatch, list the heavy validate runs in the design and mark them serial, so validate does not overlap them.
learned.evidence: validate-slice #1: 'free memory fell to 2.7 GB ... under the 3.1 GB the engine keeps free. 2 acting runs overlapped'. Validate #3 later ran C-052 in 268 s with +2.9 MB paged and +1.6 MB nonpaged.

learned.lesson: Investigation fix-direction (a), 'judge only what survives a standby purge', is refuted on created VHD sets and must not be re-adopted. Spike 106's purge re-created 0% of NtfF on the 400x40 set, and the 100x40 gate failed (NtfF +28, under the required 50). The investigation's Sandbox purge on big folders gave back -2,460. Deep pressure released the state only at Sandbox scale (SC-231). The design used neither as a discriminator and relied on warm-repeat slope instead, and spike 107 supports that: P2-P4 NtfF +0/+0/+0 on A-small, A-large and FileRepository H1. NtfF counts folders only (+401 = 400 folders plus the root); per-file state shows on Ntff.
learned.evidence: Spike 106 sandbox-purge-repeat-attribution-combined (no-go) against the investigation's Sandbox evidence; spike 107 constraints on A-large (NtfF +401 over 400,000 probes, Ntff +13,180).

learned.lesson: At medium risk with one designer, critique-review does not run (recorded as sized out, twice here), so the critique is the only pre-build model check. It ran 4 times and its 21 findings in attempt 2 were all disposed by a model and counted as untriaged. The checks it did not test for were found later by code review or the build: rule-spelling completeness, the baseline that prints no -Report text, and who discharges the must-verify preconditions. For harness slices, expect the critique's value to be in checks that cannot pass as written (N1, N2, N8), and ask it explicitly about obligation ownership and rule spelling coverage.
learned.evidence: critique-review #1 and #2: 'does not get its review reviewed'. Critique #2 and #4: 13 and 8 findings disposed by a model. The misses recorded against the critique gate in this reflection.

missed.what: The design imported 'F1 is cold' and 'the cache F1 builds survives to F2..F5' as must-verify invariants without asking who can discharge them. They became verify obligations O-044/O-045 aimed at validate, which only a person's session 1 can discharge. Critique M6 looked at the same preconditions but fixed only SC-230 and never asked what happens to an obligation no loop stage can discharge. It also did not apply lessons #344/#357 to preconditions, only to criteria.
missed.caught_by: code-review (drift note 'unless retargeted to a person, validate will hold'), then validate-slice #2 halted

missed.what: The first fitness entry's three patterns (.taad/fitness.yaml:1176-1178) carry no (?i), and the corpus spelled every operator in lower case. `$WatchedTags -Contains $_[0]`, `-In` and `-EQ` passed both entries. N3 and M1 examined this exact entry and concluded 'attempt 1's first pattern catches it' without trying a capitalised operator.

The class enumeration omitted Compare-Object and Select-String, which fold case like the Group-Object and -Unique already added. `Compare-Object @('NtfF') @('Ntff')` reports 0 differences. It is the natural way to ask which tags appeared between two marks. The critique never asked which cmdlets in the tag-reading path compare strings.

No pattern covered the quoted or indexed property spelling `$_['tag'] -eq $name`, `$_.'tag'`, `-Property 'tag'` or `switch ($row['tag'])`. That is the file's own house idiom: PoolWatch.ps1 indexes dictionaries with `$x['key']` 16 times, and Read-Mark builds entries as [ordered]@{ tag = ... }. Over live entries it returns Ntff's entry for 'NtfF' (pa 900, not 7). Code review round 1 also missed it.

The design's text comparison of -Report output with 0feac0e assumed the baseline PoolWatchCases prints -Report text. It does not: Write-Output inside Invoke-Report/Invoke-Fixture is swallowed as a return value. Critique N1 rewrote the comparison method (git archive, normalisation) and still did not check that the baseline produced any text.
missed.caught_by: build (undeclared-in-design deviation: Write-Host change and copying the tree's PoolWatchCases over the base)

lessons_judged.why: The design and record state the tens-of-GB report is not claimed fixed and that the cause of the unattributed tags is unknown. Record (b) quotes the 24.4 GB / 47.41 h source beside the 1 KB-per-path figure (m6), and Q-188 stays open.

It set the WC rule: leak tags are bounded by their own idle movement only, with no 10%-of-F1 term, so a +5-per-walk leak stays visible. N6 then corrected invariant 4 to must-verify because +5 is not above spike 107's idle 6-9.

The design filed both Restart sessions as person-run and built only the harness fix and the record. But the slice itself was not split at open and still opened as one medium bug fix. The lesson held, and validate paid for it: O-044/O-045 were imported as obligations to validate.

DONE (c), session 1 and session 2 were filed checked_by person, and no whole-C: run was attempted unattended. The gap: the 'must-verify' invariants were not person-owned, which is why validate halted on them.

It drove the P-004 design: one live Read-Mark (about 0.4 s) instead of a C-052 extension (about 5 min, +0.11 GB). It did not protect validate, whose own overlapping runs hit the engine's memory floor.

It produced M5/Get-ScratchParent in PoolWatchCases.ps1 (Write-Run and C-011) and SL-099-CasesUnderEngineTemp.Tests.ps1, which runs P-003 and P-004 under TEMP=C:\WINDOWS\TEMP. C-052's rooting and the other scripts it lists stay unfixed.

candidates.title: Commit spike 106's and the investigation's run evidence under docs/design/SL-099-runs/
candidates.why: Record claims (b), (d) and the 'no purge, no pressure step' decision rest on spike 106's five experiments: 2 go (sc130-guard-stop-survives-interrupt-fix, sandbox-deep-pressure-releases-listing-state) and 3 no-go (host-repeat-listing-keeps-no-pool, sandbox-purge-repeat-attribution-combined, sandbox-extended-tags-attribute-cold-listing). They also rest on the investigation's host and Sandbox runs (.taad-scratch/host-e1.ps1). The build's file list shows only docs/design/SL-099-runs/spike-107-2026-10-12/ (53 files, 4.2 MB); no other run folder is listed in the SL-099 build's changed-file list. Spike 87's marks.jsonl, events.log, T.json and result.txt were lost from C:\WINDOWS\TEMP, and the pool figures became uncheckable (survey: the run folder now holds only L\). Spike folders sit under %APPDATA%\taad3\spikes\8\ (path pattern from spike 107; the spike-106 location is unverified). Check which of them still exist before copying, and write missing.txt for any that are already gone.

candidates.title: PoolWatchCases: run -Report under both shells and stop Invoke-Report's Check from swallowing its ok line
candidates.why: Two code-review drift items that no backlog row holds. (1) tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1 Invoke-Report always launches `pwsh`, so P-003, P-004 and C-056 never run Get-Missing or Format-Net in Windows PowerShell 5.1. Only the SL-099 repro does, plus P-004's in-process Get-Net call. The validator proved 5.1 only with a scratch copy that swaps `& pwsh` for `& powershell.exe` (P-003, P-004, C-056, P-001 passed). (2) Invoke-Report still calls Check, which uses Write-Output inside a function whose return value is used. The 'no line carries a judgement word' ok line is never printed, though a FAIL is still counted. Get-ScratchParent also now exists in three copies (tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1, the repro, tests/window/PoolWatchCases.ps1).

unknowns: Is F1 cold, and does F1's cache survive to F2..F5, on this PC at whole-C: scale (about 830k folders and 2.4M files, 31 GB)? Spike 107 covered at most 400,000 files on a 4 GB Sandbox. Only session 1 (PoolWatch.ps1 -Prepare, a true Start > Restart, then -Protocol within 30 minutes) can answer it (SC-252, SC-253). The answer decides whether rule (d) can tell cache from leak at all.

How much do the seven WC leak tags (WCsc, WCse, WCss, WCfc, WCri, WCfn, FMwi) move at idle on this host over a 1,200 s window? The rule bounds them by idle movement only. Spike 107's Sandbox idle was 2-9, and lesson #349's leak is +5 per walk, so the rule cannot see it if the host's idle on a tag is 5 or more.

Does a live guard trip through Invoke-ExeArm write the arm-line shape the fixtures assume (guardStop, interrupted, killed false, exitCode -1)? Every SC-130 shape was exercised only through hand-built fixtures, and no live arm tripped or was interrupted in either rehearsal.

Is the tens-of-GB report this same metadata-cache mechanism, given MS Q&A 5966064 (24.4 GB combined after 47.41 h, no release)? Release under deep pressure was shown only in a 4 GB Sandbox (SC-231), and where NTFS's close cache levels off on this PC is unknown (SC-229). Q-188 stays open.

Does Ntff, rather than NtfF, carry the per-file state on the host's ntfs.sys 10.0.26100.9444? Spike 107 measured it on 10.0.26100.1 only. Session 1's F1 will show it if Ntff stays flat while files are probed.
